final_recommendation: The room collapsed without reaching settlement. FINMA offered $180M by Friday with coordinated SNB issuance and a Monday joint statement protecting AT1 hierarchy, but bondholder counsel's unilateral ultimatum to file individual board notices regardless destroyed the fragile consensus and triggered immediate market panic.
minority_objections: Insurance observer repeatedly warned that filing individual board notices Monday morning same-window as the regulatory statement would guarantee FINMA digs in rather than settles
Credit market analyst and institutional investor both conditioned settlement support on SNB closing AT1 issuance by Friday EOD, not just announcing intent
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel insisted on filing individual board notices to maximize pressure, while FINMA demanded staying the filing as precondition for settlement talks
Market participants needed visible SNB issuance by Friday to reprice AT1 spreads, but SNB's execution timeline remained ambiguous throughout
FINMA's $180M settlement offer required confidentiality and coordinated Monday announcement, but counsel refused to commit to staying supplemental filings
key_concessions: FINMA offered to waive all defenses tied to viability-language rewrite and settle at $180M by Friday COB
FINMA committed to joint Monday statement with SNB and ECB explicitly protecting AT1 hierarchy across all three regulatory frameworks
Bondholder counsel initially agreed to explore settlement discussions if FINMA engaged by Wednesday EOD
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: would not stay individual board-naming filings as precondition for settlement talks
FINMA: required written commitment from counsel to stay supplemental notices through Friday before engaging settlement negotiations
Institutional investor: would not reprice AT1 holdings unless SNB closed and funded issuance by Friday EOD, not just announced intent
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room never resolved whether SNB had final credit approval and pricing locked for Friday close—all settlement pressure hinged on this unverified assumption
No participant addressed how a $180M settlement would be allocated across the bondholder group or whether all holders would accept the terms
The room did not model what happens if FINMA's D&O carriers deny coverage during the settlement window, potentially forcing the board to fund $180M personally
downstream_risk_variables: SNB AT1 issuance execution and pricing by Friday EOD
FINMA's D&O carrier coverage decisions on retroactive-act and gross negligence exclusions
Market repricing of AT1 spreads across all systemically important issuers post-Monday statement
Reinsurance cascade if primary D&O carriers deny and excess layers get triggered
Bondholder group internal consensus on accepting $180M settlement versus continuing litigation
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated without resolving: (1) whether SNB would actually close AT1 issuance by Friday EOD or merely signal intent; (2) whether FINMA's board could secure D&O carrier approval for $180M settlement payment before Friday; (3) whether bondholder counsel's threat to file individual notices regardless was negotiating posture or genuine intent; (4) how the broader AT1 market would react to a confidential settlement versus public litigation.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Bondholder counsel drove the entire meeting toward multi-jurisdiction filing with discovery demands, E&O notices, and individual board-naming—litigation was the dominant path throughout, culminating in counsel's refusal to stay filings even for settlement talks.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: The room's central legal theory was that FINMA retrofitted viability language post-facto via the March 19 ordinance—bondholder counsel repeatedly framed discovery as exposing 'intent to redefine, not apply' and targeted gross negligence in the viability-language rewrite.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion was mentioned as market concern and precedent risk, but the room's energy focused more on litigation mechanics and settlement pressure than on developing the hierarchy controversy as a standalone legal or contagion theory.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing, spread blow-outs, and the need for coordinated SNB issuance to restore confidence dominated every round—participants repeatedly conditioned settlement support on visible market action, not just legal memos.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The 3-5 year multi-jurisdiction discovery tail, D&O defense costs ($15-18M annually), reinsurance cascade, and uninsured board exposure were developed in granular detail across every round—this was a central, structured risk driving settlement urgency.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O carrier coverage denials, retroactive-act exclusions, E&O exposure for SNB advisers, reinsurance accumulation, and personal board liability were dissected in every round—financial-lines exposure was a primary lever for settlement pressure and a concrete downstream risk.
